points.title: What normalisation is
points.must: Organising data into well-structured related tables following the normal forms so each fact is stored once, redundancy is reduced and anomalies are avoided.

points.title: Redundancy and anomalies
points.must: Data redundancy explained, and the update, insertion and deletion anomalies, each with an example.

points.title: Benefits and drawbacks
points.must: At least two: less redundancy / storage, consistent data (change in one place), no anomalies, easier to maintain. Drawback: More tables so queries need joins (can be slower / more complex); some systems denormalise for speed.

points.title: Rules of 1NF, 2NF and 3NF
points.must: The rule of each normal form in order: 1NF atomic values and no repeating groups with a primary key; 2NF no partial dependency on part of a composite key; 3NF no transitive dependency on a non-key field.

points.title: Key terms
points.must: Atomic value, repeating group, composite key, functional dependency (A → B) — each with an example.

points.title: Full, partial and transitive dependency
points.must: One example of each, e.g. (StudentID, SubjectID) → Mark; StudentID → StudentName; Class → ClassTeacher; which form each breaks.

points.title: Converting to 1NF
points.must: Make values atomic (one row per value / split fields), remove repeating groups, choose a primary key — often composite.

points.title: Converting to 2NF
points.must: Move fields that depend on part of the key into a new table with that part as its primary key; keep it in the original table as a foreign key.

points.title: Converting to 3NF
points.must: Move the dependent fields to a new table; the field they depend on becomes its primary key and stays as a foreign key in the original table.

points.title: Notation
points.must: Primary keys underlined, foreign keys marked with *; table written as TableName(Field1, Field2, …).

points.title: A full worked example
points.must: An unnormalised table (e.g. the club register) taken step by step to 1NF, 2NF and 3NF with the final tables and keys.

points.title: Link (junction) table
points.must: Resolves a many-to-many relationship; its primary key is the composite of the two foreign keys, e.g. Memberships(PupilID*, ClubID*).

points.title: Steps to create the database
points.must: Create tables with data types, set primary keys, create foreign keys, create the “one” tables first, enter test data, test with join queries.

points.title: Referential integrity
points.must: Every foreign key value must match an existing primary key value; an insert with a non-existent class is rejected.

points.title: CREATE TABLE with keys
points.must: SQL with PRIMARY KEY, REFERENCES Table(Field), NOT NULL, and a composite PRIMARY KEY (a, b).
